1) The sink is std::cout << ... << std::endl, which simply writes to the console and does not invoke an operating‑system shell or execute commands.
2) No subsequent code or function calls (e.g., system(), exec(), popen()) are present that would use the printed data as a command.
3) The untrusted data is only displayed; there is no transformation or execution path.
4) Even if the data contains shell metacharacters, std::cout treats them as ordinary characters and does not perform command interpretation.
5) Therefore, there is no path from the untrusted source to an OS command execution primitive.
